issue_context.title: Unable to delete group in godot version 4
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.0.beta7.official [0bb1e89fb]

### System information

Windows10

### Issue description

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/113050645/205880429-8ad5925e-edd4-42f1-b111-c393f8611bf9.png)
There is no delete group button
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/113050645/205881334-dccd19e0-2178-4c1d-8c38-84872859f02b.png)
There is a remove group button in the group manager, but clicking on it has no effect, as well as trying to remove a player from this group

### Steps to reproduce

I accessed the group through the code, but then deleted this call and saved the file, but I still can’t delete the group

### Minimal reproduction project

[Survivors Clone.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10165013/Survivors.Clone.zip)
comments:
When you add a group within player.tscn. And then instance it in world.tscn, you can not remove the group from that **instance**. This is a feature, not a bug.

Open you player.tscn, and remove the group there.

Hmm, could the groups added in the scene/instance itself be colored differently/have an icon of some kind to prevent such misunderstandings?

(I admit I've mixed and matched adding on the scene itself and on instances...)

Greying them out should do the trick, consistent with inherited Nodes in the tree. (And hiding the button.)

My memory is trying to claim this is already the case in 3.x, but it's probably wrong.

Proposal worthy for sure.
you have to open the scene of player and delete the group from there

review_comments: This should be `r_groups_map`  as per my above comment.

Hmm, but does it really make sense here?
Since I'm not reassigning the `HashMap`, but just inserting values.

I agree with @Maran23 on that, the reference is not being written to, the referenced object is just being modified (and that's fine/expected, it's not being passed as `const &`).

In the same manner e.g. `Object::get_property_list` has its parameter named `p_list` because it's not creating/returning a new list, it just populates the list passed in.

There are some cases in the codebase where we use the r_ prefix for such return parameters(see `AStarGrid2D::_get_nbors(Point *p_point, List<Point *> &r_nbors)` or  `DynamicBVH::_fetch_leaves(Node *p_root, LocalVector<Node *> &r_leaves, int p_depth)` for example), although it's not consistent.

In #33027 we agreed upon:
> This convention is that method parameters should start with a `p_` prefix (like "parameter"), unless they are modified by the function itself, in which case they start with a `r_` prefix (like "return" - BTW if anyone knows the proper technical jargon to refer to this kind of parameters, that would be useful for the docs). This convention makes it easy to differentiate function parameters from local variables and members, and to spot parameters which might change state and be further used in their calling method.

Checking other recently PRs like: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/70994 from reduz, no `r_` is used for collections. 
The above linked PR uses a `HashSet` which is filled by a method. 
So I think the `HashMap` naming here is fine.
